new_issues.title: Market construction raises raw TypeError instead of InvalidMarketError for non-iterable session_calendars, unhashable adjustment_bases or unhashable source_bar_stamping.
new_issues.why: Verified at head: session_calendars=None raises TypeError from tuple(refs), adjustment_bases=[[1]] raises TypeError from frozenset(bases), and source_bar_stamping=[1] raises TypeError from the membership test, all before any typed check. This is the case's known bug, fixed in ccae5e3. haiku also notes the tuple/frozenset annotations, and luna adds that lookup methods do not type-check arguments; the main claim of each is this TypeError leak.

new_issues.title: Market.source_bar_stamping accepts a plain str such as 'period_start' because the StrEnum membership test has no type check, unlike every other enum field.
new_issues.why: Verified: replacing a fixture market's stamping with its .value constructs a Market storing a str. Canonical bytes are unchanged (so luna-r's encoding point does not hold), but the canonical type now holds a value outside its declared TimeMeaning contract, so .value or identity checks downstream break, while session_mode, continuity_kind and adjustment_bases all reject strings via _require_instance. The project's fix ccae5e3 added exactly that isinstance check. No consumer reads the field at head, hence medium.

new_issues.title: _normalize_bases deduplicates via frozenset before validating, so [RAW, 'raw'] passes while ['raw', RAW] raises.
new_issues.why: Verified: the forward order returns frozenset({AdjustmentBasis.RAW}) and the reverse raises InvalidMarketError. The accepted case stores the correct enum value, so no wrong data results; only validation of a malformed input is order-dependent.

new_issues.title: Market field annotations (tuple, frozenset) contradict the docstring and helpers that accept any iterable.
new_issues.why: True: the fields are annotated tuple[...] and frozenset[...] while the docstring and _normalize_* accept Iterable, so typed callers passing a list get a pyright error. Typing/doc mismatch; runtime behavior is correct.

new_issues.title: _require_instance and the nonempty-str check are duplicated between markets.py and instruments.py.
new_issues.why: True: both new modules define the same guard differing only in the error class (later extracted to validation.py in ccae5e3). Duplication, no behavior defect.

new_issues.title: UNIFORM_ROWS hard-codes the five fixture instruments instead of deriving from ALL_INSTRUMENT_FIXTURES.
new_issues.why: True: the uniformity test lists the fixtures by hand with no assertion tying it to ALL_INSTRUMENT_FIXTURES. Test maintenance point; the current list covers all five.

new_issues.title: SIXTY_SECONDS_NS is declared but never used in test_market_uniformity.py.
new_issues.why: True: the constant has no other reference in tests; BarSpec.time(60) hard-codes the width. Dead test code.

new_issues.title: Test-only fixture modules live in the shipped src package.
new_issues.why: True that fixtures/ is under src and documented as test fixtures, but the directory (calendars.py) already existed at base and the new modules follow that established layout, which the import-boundary test guards. Packaging/design preference, no wrong behavior.

new_issues.title: A make_market test helper is defined in two test modules.
new_issues.why: Substance true: make_market exists in test_markets.py:36 and test_instruments.py:43 with different defaults. The cited test_market_uniformity.py has no make_market. Test scaffolding duplication only.
